summary: The prepared source already contains unconditional recovery of all-NaN DSPARK draft probability rows to a token-0 one-hot distribution before torch.multinomial. Added regression and boundary coverage; no production-path source correction was justified.

tests.what_was_measured: Three CPU tests: unrecovered NaN probabilities reproduce torch.multinomial's probability-tensor failure; all-minus-infinity and positive-infinity softmax rows recover to token zero; valid rows remain unchanged.

On gfx950, two non-finite softmax rows became finite token-0 one-hot rows and torch.multinomial completed; a valid row matched an independently computed float64 CPU softmax reference. Raw output: reports/j-770cd9dc90ea/raw/gpu_dspark_probability_recovery.txt

gpu_execution.evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950:sramecc+:xnack- with torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2; recovery, sampling, synchronization, and CPU-reference comparison completed on cuda:0.

remaining_limitations: The assigned environment has one AMD gfx950 GPU, not eight NVIDIA H100 GPUs with CUDA.
TP=8, the full serving path, week-long production traffic, and the intermittent root cause that creates non-finite logits were not reproduced.
This verifies containment at the implicated DSPARK multinomial boundary, not model semantic accuracy or distributed behavior.
